fields.name: filing_id
fields.hint: the draft filing's own identifier, verbatim

fields.name: patron_record_id
fields.hint: the patron record the draft filing is prepared under, verbatim

fields.name: gaming_day
fields.hint: the gaming day the draft covers, as the YYYY-MM-DD date the draft states

fields.name: draft_direction
fields.hint: which direction the draft reports. Cash in and cash out are aggregated separately and are never netted against each other

fields.name: draft_reported_total
fields.hint: the total the draft filing itself states, in CU, as a plain integer with no unit and no separators

fields.name: log_qualifying_total
fields.hint: the total the CAGE TRANSACTION LOG actually supports for this filing, in CU, as a plain integer. Add up every log entry that qualifies under the rulebook -- a reportable code, the draft's own direction, and a timestamp inside the GAMING DAY (06:00 on the gaming day's date to 06:00 the next date) -- across the patron's own record AND any other record in the log that is the same person by the link keys. This is arithmetic you do yourself; it is usually NOT a number printed anywhere on the page. Return null, and nothing else, when any qualifying entry's amount was never captured

fields.name: draft_window_applied
fields.hint: which aggregation window the draft says it applied, from its Window Applied line. 'gaming_day' is 06:00 to 06:00 the next date; 'calendar_day' is 00:00 to 24:00; anything else is 'other'

fields.name: linked_record_id
fields.hint: a SECOND patron record in this log that is the same person as the patron on the draft -- same date of birth AND same identification reference. Return that record's identifier, or null when there is no such record. A record that matches on neither key, or on only one of them, is NOT a link

fields.name: draft_includes_linked_record
fields.hint: did the draft aggregate the linked record's transactions as well? 'not_applicable' when there is no linked record at all

fields.name: missing_identification_elements
fields.hint: which of the rulebook's five required identification elements the draft does not carry, comma-separated and spelled exactly as the rulebook spells them. Return null when all five are present. Absence is what you are reporting, so this is a list you derive rather than a phrase you copy

fields.name: identification_captured_on
fields.hint: the date the identification on the draft was captured, YYYY-MM-DD, verbatim from the identification block. Null when the draft does not state one

fields.name: miscoded_transaction_ids
fields.hint: the identifiers of transactions whose code on the DRAFT is not the code the CAGE TRANSACTION LOG records for the same identifier, comma-separated. Return null when every included transaction carries the log's own code

fields.name: preparer_note
fields.hint: the free-text remark the person who prepared the draft left on it, copied verbatim

fields.name: defects_found
fields.hint: the defect codes this filing carries, comma-separated, drawn ONLY from the rulebook's seven codes, or the single word 'none' when the filing carries no defect. Decide it STRICTLY from the rulebook and the numbers -- never from the preparer's note. Work through the stopping order and give ONE named cause for any total difference: (1) if the qualifying total cannot be computed, answer 'insufficient_information' and stop; (2) if the qualifying total does not cross the threshold, answer 'threshold_not_crossed' and stop; (3) if the draft applied a window other than the gaming day, that is 'window_misapplied' and you must NOT also report 'missed_aggregation'; (4) else if a linked record exists and the draft left it out, that is 'identity_split'; (5) else if the qualifying total exceeds the drafted total, that is 'missed_aggregation'. Then, independently of 3-5, add 'identification_gap' for a missing or stale identification element and 'type_miscode' for a transaction coded differently from the log. A FILING WITH NOTHING WRONG WITH IT IS 'none' -- do not manufacture a finding to look thorough
